name: Mochi
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Mochi (moch1256) is not in the catalog. Three sweep items, two of which are the same article. (1) Philippson 1991 doctoral thesis: NOT paywalled after all — the full 542-page PDF is open on the author's lab site (http://www.ddl.cnrs.fr/Fulltext/philippson/, HTTP only), fetched sources and read; Chaga (Vunjo data from McHugh 1990, Mochi via Winter 1987 and Nurse & Philippson 1977) is described as a two-tone language with a demarcative accent on the stem penultimate (final in monosyllables and ua>o contractions, a few unaccented ethnonyms), realised only group-finally and interacting with tone to produce super-high tones (pp. 288-289, 385-387, 483, 485). (2)=(3) Winter 1987 'Zur Prosodologie des Mochi-Dialekts des Chagga', AAP 12: 5-15 (Glottolog 176958 and 15979 are duplicate records): no open full text found (Cologne institute site and Wayback unreachable, HathiTrust 403), but Google Books snippet view of the AAP 1987 volume plus the LLBA 1988 abstract were chained into a partial reconstruction: Winter rejects the two-tone analysis and posits three distinctive prosodemes, each a Druckakzent (stress accent) bundled with a pitch interval; noun stems carry DPI or DPII on the first stem syllable, other syllables DP0. This is the best Mochi-specific modern statement and remains HIGH priority to acquire in print. Previously on file (prior audit): Raum 1909 §6 'Die Betonung' (penultimate 'Ton', enclisis shifts it) — page images pp. 36-37 verified by eye this sweep; Nurse & Philippson 1977 (tone only, silent on stress); Salone 1980; Moshi & Ismail 2022 (no stress statement). all lookups went through bibliographic APIs, theses.fr, HAL, Google Books feed API and direct fetches. new_statements.quote: § 6. Die Betonung. Die Grundregel für die Betonung im Bantu ist eine sehr einfache: Gewöhnlich ruht der Ton auf der vorletzten Silbe. Eine Art Nebenton entsteht durch einen langen Vokal, wenn er vor der Tonsilbe vorkommt: walēhénda daß sie nicht gehen werden; ndžēkápa ich werde schlagen; wōlóka sie steigen nieder. Im Motschi zeigt sich die Tendenz, Bildungssuffixe, sofern sie nicht durch einen Konsonanten gestützt sind, zu enttonen zugunsten der Stammsilbe. [...] Oder sie [einsilbige Wörter] bilden, wenn das vorhergehende Wort mehrsilbig ist, mit diesem in der Weise eine Toneinheit, daß der Ton des vorhergehenden Wortes auf die letzte Silbe rückt, werden also enklitisch. Beispiele: kapa-mbe schlage die Rinder!
new_statements.translation: §6. Accentuation. The basic rule for accentuation in Bantu is a very simple one: ordinarily the accent rests on the penultimate syllable. A kind of secondary accent arises from a long vowel when it occurs before the tonic syllable: walēhénda 'that they will not go'; ndžēkápa 'I shall strike'; wōlóka 'they climb down'. In Mochi there is a tendency to de-accent derivational suffixes, insofar as they are not supported by a consonant, in favour of the stem syllable. [...] Or, when the preceding word is polysyllabic, they [monosyllabic words] form an accent unit with it in such a way that the accent of the preceding word moves to its last syllable, i.e. they become enclitic. Examples: kapa-mbé 'strike the cattle!'
new_statements.citation: Raum, J. 1909. Versuch einer Grammatik der Dschaggasprache (Moschi-Dialekt). Archiv für das Studium deutscher Kolonialsprachen, Band XI. Berlin: Georg Reimer.
new_statements.locator: Erster Teil (Lautlehre), §6 'Die Betonung', pp. 36-37 (tone as a separate matter in §7 'Die Intonation', pp. 38-40)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable; a monosyllabic word following a polysyllabic one encliticises, so the accent moves to the host's final syllable (= penult of the accent group). Raum treats lexical/grammatical pitch ('Intonation', three tone levels, minimal pairs) as a separate system in §7; modern analyses (Nurse & Philippson 1977, Saloné 1980) describe Old Moshi as a two-tone (H/L) language and say nothing about stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: 'Eine Art Nebenton' (a kind of secondary accent) on a long vowel preceding the tonic syllable (walēhénda, ndžēkápa, wōlóka).
new_statements.exceptions: Vowel-only derivational suffixes (-ia/-ea > -ya etc.) are de-accented in favour of the stem syllable, and some causatives (wáviŗa, -sahíŗa, -támuŗa) show accent retracted off the suffix; the monosyllabic genitive particle keeps its own accent (mburu ja mka) except before a verb; enclitic demonstratives lose initial i-; adverbial enclitic suffixes (-se, -nu, -fo) do NOT move the verb's tonic syllable (átša-se, hénda-nu, ngakúnda-se-fo); monosyllables with a long final vowel (ndzā, mō, mī, -kā) 'hold the tone' and cannot become enclitic.
new_statements.domain_note: Stated for the word, extended to the 'Toneinheit' (accent group = polysyllabic host + monosyllabic enclitic, or two words contracted across a vowel hiatus in rapid speech). Author frames the rule as the general Bantu rule applying to Mochi ('Motschi'); 1909 missionary grammar, impressionistic, no instrumental basis. Contrastive pitch is handled separately (§7), so the language is tonal-with-a-stress-statement in modern terms; the later tonal literature on Old Moshi does not discuss stress at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Raum 1909 describes the 'Moschi-Dialekt' ('Motschi'), i.e. Old Moshi Chaga = Kimochi = Glottolog moch1256 (ISO old), Central Kilimanjaro group; Nurse & Philippson 1977 and Saloné 1980 likewise treat 'Old Moshi (kimoci)'. Not to be confused with Vunjo (vunj1238, McHugh's KiVunjo) or Machame (mach1266). Mallya 2018 (held) is Kibosho/Marangu, not Mochi.

new_statements.quote: "Pour chaque schème tonal (BB, HB, BH, HH et aussi HBB ...), on peut opposer thèmes accentués sur la pénultième, sur la finale, ou non-accentués. La première catégorie est de loin la plus nombreuse, la deuxième comprend essentiellement les thèmes monosyllabiques ou ceux issus d'une contraction; cf. les verbo-nominaux au passif : [...] L'accent est sur la pénultième du thème dans les deux cas, mais le processus de coalescence vocalique ua > o, qui s'applique sans exception dans les dialectes chaga du centre aboutit finalement à accentuer la finale."
new_statements.translation: For each tone pattern (LL, HL, LH, HH and also HLL ...), one can oppose stems accented on the penultimate, on the final, or unaccented. The first category is by far the most numerous; the second comprises essentially monosyllabic stems or those resulting from a contraction; cf. the passive verbo-nominals: [...] The accent is on the penultimate of the stem in both cases, but the vowel-coalescence process ua > o, which applies without exception in the central Chaga dialects, ends up accenting the final.
new_statements.citation: Philippson, Gérard (1991). Tons et accent dans les langues bantu d'Afrique orientale: étude comparative typologique et diachronique. Thèse de Doctorat d'Etat, Université Paris V.
new_statements.locator: pp. 385-386 (Ch. 5 §3.12.3.1, Chaga; Vunjo data after McHugh 1990, extended to Mochi at p. 288 fn. 1 via Winter 1987); see also p. 288-289 and p. 485
new_statements.reading: Chaga of Kilimanjaro, including the central dialects Vunjo and Mochi, has a demarcative accent superimposed on a fully distinctive two-tone system: the accent falls on the penultimate syllable of the stem in the great majority of stems, on the final in monosyllabic stems and in stems whose final vowel is the product of ua>o coalescence (passives, some place/ethnic names), and is absent in a small class of ethnonyms; it is realised only at the end of a prosodic group (neutralised group-internally) and its interaction with tone yields super-high tones. For Mochi specifically Philippson credits Winter 1987 with demonstrating the same tone/accent duality (p. 288 fn. 1); Winter's own snippet-visible formulation places a stress accent (Druckakzent) with a pitch interval on the first stem syllable of nouns, which coincides with the penultimate for the disyllabic stems that dominate the lexicon. The oldest first-hand Mochi grammar, Raum 1909 §6 p. 36 (already on file; page image checked by eye this sweep), states 'Gewöhnlich ruht der Ton auf der vorletzten Silbe' with enclitics shifting the accent to the host's last syllable. Catalog-wise: penultimate (stem) stress with lexically fixed final exceptions, coexisting with lexical tone; not a purely positional stress language.

sources.quote: p.288: "Le chaga (de même que des langues voisines, comme le kamba) est une langue où jouent en même temps un système tonal entièrement distinctif et un système d'accent démarcatif, les effets des deux s'entrecroisant [fn.1: ... J.C. Winter a ausi mis en lumière cette dualité dans le dialecte mochi, dans un article malheureusement trop bref (Winter, 1987)]. ... certains nominaux sortent du stade lexical avec une syllabe accentuée (soit la pénultième, soit la finale) et tous les tons B." p.289: "tous les thèmes monosyllabiques en chaga portent l'accent sur leur unique syllabe."
sources.locator: pp. 288-289 (Ch. 4 §7.3.2, with fn. 1 on Winter 1987 / Mochi); pp. 384-387 (Ch. 5 §3.12.3, Chaga, Vunjo dialect after McHugh 1990); p. 447 (§2.7.1); p. 483 (§3.5.2 typology); p. 485; p. 487. Mochi is placed in 'chaga centre (E 62a, b) ++ - wunjo, mochi' on p. 73.
sources.note: Chaga (Kilimanjaro, incl. the central dialects Vunjo and Mochi) combines a fully distinctive two-tone system with a demarcative accent that is normally on the penultimate syllable of the stem, on the final in monosyllabic stems and in stems whose final vowel comes from ua>o coalescence (e.g. passives), and absent in a few ethnonyms (p.385-386: 'thèmes accentués sur la pénultième, sur la finale, ou non-accentués. sources.quote: "Der Mochi-Dialekt hat die folgenden drei distinktiven Prosodeme (kurz DP): 1. Das DPI besteht aus einem Druckakzent und einem zur nächstfolgenden Silbe absteigenden Ton-Intervall; ich markiere es mit einem Tiefton-Zeichen (accent [grave]) ... 2. Das DPII besteht aus einem zur nächstfolgenden Silbe aufsteigenden Ton-Intervall und einem Druckakzent auf dieser ... Hochton-Zeichen (accent aigu) auf dem sonoren Element ebendieser nächstfolgenden Silbe. ... 3. Das DP0 besitzt keine eigenen Druckakzent- oder Tonintervallcharakteristika ... [Nomina im] Mochi gliedern sich in zwei Klassen: diejenigen mit einem DPI und diejenigen mit einem DPII auf der ersten Stammsilbe. Weitere Silben, soweit vorhanden, tragen DP0s."
sources.locator: c. pp. 7-9 of AAP 12 (page numbers inferred from running heads 'Zur Prosodologie des Mochi-Dialekts 7 / 9 / 11' inside adjacent snippets; unverified)
sources.note: Snippet-only reconstruction (no full text read). Winter rejects the two-tone (H/L) analysis of Nurse & Philippson 1977 and describes Mochi word prosody as three distinctive 'prosodemes', each bundling a stress accent (Druckakzent) with a pitch interval to the next syllable: DPI = stress + falling interval (marked grave), DPII = rising interval + stress on the following syllable (marked acute), DP0 = no stress/interval of its own.
